title: Ayurveda in India vs Abroad: The Truth
description:
Ayurveda is often marketed as an ancient, miracle system of medicine. But when you look closely at the facts, the double standards become glaring. In India, Ayurvedic companies loudly claim that their powders, oils, and pills cure everything from diabetes to arthritis. Yet the very same companies, when selling in the US or Europe, are forced to label them as “food supplements” that cannot cure, diagnose, or prevent any disease.

Why? Because strict scientific regulations abroad demand evidence. Without randomized controlled trials, molecular studies, and long-term safety data, no system can be called medicine. Western regulatory bodies treat lives as valuable — they don’t allow pseudoscience to be marketed as cures. Meanwhile, in India, the government goes as far as creating a ministry to promote these pseudoscientific products, even while people risk their health.

This video exposes how Ayurvedic giants play both sides: selling unproven remedies as “medicine” to Indians, but downgrading them to “supplements” abroad to avoid legal trouble. It highlights the hypocrisy, the exploitation of belief, and the lack of consumer protection at home.

If you’ve searched for Ayurveda truth, Ayurvedic scam, Ayurveda in USA vs India, herbal medicine fraud, food supplement scam, pseudoscience in Ayurveda, or Ayurveda debunked, this video lays out the evidence.

Like, comment, share, and hype this video so more people understand the double standards and demand science-based medicine.

comments.text:
Dear Anand, I recently stumbled upon your videos and I am happy to see a sane voice on the internet, especially on the maida video. However I beg to differ on this case

Let me give you one example from personal experience. My dad had asthma, and his grandmother advised him to take "Vasha Arishtam" for it. Remember at that time there was no commercialization of ayurveda, so if you want it, you had to make it. Recipes were time (and crowd) tested. If it does not work, it will not be passed on. It worked for him. The main component of that preparation was a plant called Malabar Nut (used to be Adhatoda Vasaca, now called Justicia adhatoda). In a pinch I have seen my dad just adding chopped up malabar nut leaves to boiling water and drinking it, which worked for him. Later, I also developed asthma, and being a scientific temper guy, I did not bother with all these and went straight to an allopathic doctor. Many years and many doctors later I settled on one drug which works for me - Bromhexine. Fast forward a few years, I realized that this drug was developed by a german company - Boehringer Ingelheim originally from Malabar nut plant in the 60s, and that plant contains more than 1% bromhexine by dry weight. So well, amy I going back to chopping malabar nut leaves, no. This drug is available cheaply, and is scientifically proven, so why should I not use it. But in a pinch, I know where to look.

But what about pre 1966? science and allopathy did not have this cure for asthma, but our ancestors did! What about pre 1600AD? they were prescribing whiskey, while we still had "Vasha Arishtam". See I am not saying that we reject english medicine and take ayurveda for heart attack. Stick to known good methods where they work, But if allopathy does not have a treatment and can only support you symptomatically while there is a time tested medicine in Ayurveda, then why not?

I am not advertising for all these commercial interests that is trying to make money by commodifying ayurveda. I am only saying that do not see ayurveda as what these companies are putting in front of you. It is a body of knowledge that our ancestors have been testing and improving for a really long time.

Sorry to write a long essay here, but let me give you one example where the scientific method took its own sweet time to catch up: The native Americans always treated corn with lime in a process now called Nixtamalization. We now know that this helps reduce toxins and makes the vitamins in corn bioavailable. The modern English settlers did not bother to do this (may be due to lack of then scientific evidence) and this led to lack of niacin among them and pellagra being endemic among them. My point is time tested methods are there for a reason, and rather than dismissing them as unscientific and quackery, we should lead in researching our traditional knowledge rather than waiting for Europeans to come and research it for us.
